title: Weight-Loss Medication Changes What People Buy to Wear

source.author: Renan Botelho de Carvalho
source.title: How weight-loss drugs are reshaping wardrobe spending

paragraphs: New medication helps many people lose excess weight. It also changes how they shop for clothes. This is the finding of new research from Circana, a company that studies what people buy. FashionUnited reported on it on November 12, 2026.

Circana looked at what families in the United States bought between August 2023 and July 2026. It chose families where at least one person takes weight-loss medication and started between 2024 and 2026. Then it compared them with families that never used it.

How does Circana measure the change? It gives each kind of clothing a score. The score shows how much a family spends, compared with the 12 months before the medication began. The numbers below are points on this score. They are not percent increases in sales. Year one means the first 12 months of treatment. Year two means months 13 to 24.

For clothing as a whole, the score was 2.9 points higher in year one. In year two, it was 6.4 points higher. So the duration of treatment matters. People did not stop after the first few months. They went on filling the closet.

Two kinds of clothing did very well. The first is clothes for swimming. In year one, the swim score was only 1.7 points higher. In year two, it was 15.5 points higher. That is a remarkable jump. The second is outdoor clothing, such as coats and jackets. Its score rose from 10.9 points to 15 points. Sweaters also did well. Their score went from 6.8 to 14.9 points.
Not everything changed. Spending on shoes stayed close to the old level. It was 0.1 points lower in year one and 0.2 points lower in year two.

What triggers the shopping? Circana asked people in September 2026. In families where someone takes the medication, 43% said they had bought clothing or shoes in the past three months because of it. The most common trigger was a change in size, at 28%. Then came a wish for a new style, at 18%. New activities came third, at 13%. In other words, people do not only need smaller clothes. Some also start a new lifestyle and dress differently.

Nevertheless, the research has limits. It does not explain exactly why outdoor and swim clothes grew more than other kinds. The result is still useful for fashion companies. Circana says stores should not look only at the first months of treatment. The whole duration matters. It also says stores could be more flexible when they plan sizes. A flexible plan helps when buyers change size during the year.
The research highlights one more thing. An old shopping habit can change when the body changes. When excess weight goes, many people shop differently. A new lifestyle often needs a new closet.
